Recommended Highlights This Week

1. The Weeknd – After Hours Til Dawn Stadium Tour – 2–3 October, National Stadium (major traffic impact both nights)

2. Grand Prix Season Singapore (GPSS) 2026 begins – 2 October, citywide (Music Matters Live at Clarke Quay, Gran Turismo World Series at Marina Bay Sands)

3. Octoburst! 2026 – 2–4 October, Esplanade (free Children's Day festival)

4. TLM Food Expo – 2–4 October, Singapore EXPO Hall 6A/6B (last edition of 2026)

5. Rose Veranda's Hong Kong Cha Chaan Teng series – final weekend, closes 4 October

F&B Promotions

Current dining promotions across our Shangri-La Group properties in Singapore:

Shangri-La Singapore

Beng Hiang's residency at the Garden Terrace continues, still turning out the 48-year-old Hokkien institution's signature dishes – the Cherry Wood Charcoal-Roasted Boneless Suckling Pig and Slow-Braised Pork Belly with Steamed Bun remain the ones regulars ask for by name. Elsewhere, The Line moves into the Guangzhou leg of its Journey Across China's Culinary Heartlands from 28 September to 11 October, following on from Chengdu. Over at Shang Palace, A Cantonese Expression of Korea's Finest continues through 14 October. And it's the final weekend for The Rose Veranda's Hong Kong series – both the Cha Chaan Teng Mini Buffet and the accompanying Hi-Tea Wine Flight close on 4 October.

  • Beng Hiang – Authentic Hokkien Cuisine, Garden Terrace. Lunch 11:30am–2:30pm, Dinner 6:00pm–9:30pm, daily. No dated promotion currently advertised on the restaurant's own listing; ask guests to check with the outlet directly for any seasonal offers, since Beng Hiang runs as an independent partner residency and doesn't appear on the hotel's own F&B outlet sheet.

  • The Line – A Journey Across China's Culinary Heartlands (Guangzhou leg). Lunch from $48++/adult, $24++/child (Mon–Fri); $68++/adult, $34++/child (weekend). Dinner from $68++/adult, $34++/child (Mon–Fri); $98++/adult, $49++/child (weekend). Shangri-La Circle members: 30% off. Valid 28 September – 11 October 2026.

  • Shang Palace – A Cantonese Expression of Korea's Finest, daily lunch and dinner. Valid through 14 October 2026.

  • The Rose Veranda – Discover Hong Kong: Cha Chaan Teng Mini Buffet, Thu–Sun, $58++/adult, $29++/child; paired Hi-Tea Wine Flight from $35++. Last weekend – valid through 4 October 2026 only.

Shangri-La Rasa Sentosa

  • Rasa Private Beach BBQ – SGD 188++ per package (2 adults + 2 children). Valid through 31 December 2026.

Hotel Jen Tanglin

  • J65 – International Seafood Dinner Buffet. $88++/adult, $44++/child. Shangri-La Circle members: 20% off.

Hotel Jen Orchard Gateway

  • Makan@JEN – daily lunch and dinner buffet, $30–55++ per person. 15% off for OCBC cardmembers, ongoing.

Events & Festivals

Overall Summary

Grand Prix Season Singapore (GPSS) kicks off its 17th edition on 2 October – ten days of citywide race-season programming ahead of the Formula 1 weekend on 9–11 October – with Music Matters Live and the Gran Turismo World Series both landing inside this edition's window. The concert calendar is unusually heavy too: The Weeknd brings his stadium tour to National Stadium for two nights (2–3 October), with Itzy, Xlov, Shaggy and Bang Yong-guk also playing across the week. Families have Esplanade's free Octoburst! Children's Day festival on 2 October, and it's a food-and-technology kind of week besides: TLM Food Expo returns to Singapore EXPO for its last edition of 2026, running alongside the Smart Home Tech Show at Suntec, while ERDINGER's Oktoberfest celebrations continue island-wide. It's also the last weekend for a run of September-dated promotions and exhibitions – worth flagging the closing dates below before guests miss them.

Grand Prix Season Singapore (GPSS) 2026

Singapore Tourism Board's citywide race-season programme returns for its 17th edition, running ten days ahead of and through the Formula 1 Singapore Airlines Singapore Grand Prix (9–11 October). Two pieces land inside this edition's window: Music Matters Live, a free outdoor music festival at CQ @ Clarke Quay running 2–4 October; and the Gran Turismo World Series Round 3 at Sands Theatre, Marina Bay Sands on 3 October – marking Singapore's first-ever stop as a Southeast Asian host for the championship. The wider GPSS programme (Orchard Paddock, Ray-Ban's Beyond the Track at Clarke Quay, Porsche's Raceborn Fest) continues to build through the following week.

Event Date: 2–11 October 2026 (Music Matters Live: 2–4 Oct; Gran Turismo World Series: 3 Oct)
Location: Citywide – Orchard Road, Clarke Quay, Marina Bay, Suntec City and other precincts
Admission: Free (Music Matters Live); ticketed for Gran Turismo World Series
Best For: Motorsport Fans / Nightlife / Music Lovers

Concierge Recommendation: A good early flag for guests staying through race week – GPSS gives them race-season atmosphere without needing a circuit ticket, and Clarke Quay is a five-minute cab from the hotel for the Music Matters Live weekend.

Octoburst! 2026

Esplanade's annual, largely free Children's Day festival returns with a “Stories” theme, including two new commissions and a children's choir opening the day. Friday 2 October is the main public day (Children's Day, a school holiday); “A Universe in Sounds” continues through the weekend.

Event Date: 2–4 October 2026 (main day: 2 October)
Location: Esplanade – Theatres on the Bay
Admission: Free
Best For: Families / Young Children

Concierge Recommendation: A strong recommendation for families in-house over the Children's Day weekend – free, easy to combine with a Marina Bay stroll, and a nice contrast to the more adult-skewed GPSS programming happening the same weekend.

TLM Food Expo

One of Singapore's largest food expos returns for its final 2026 edition, spread across two weekends (25–27 September and 2–4 October). Over 200 exhibitors bring local and international brands together under one roof, with discounts of up to 90% off, $1 snacks, and more than 30 brands making their TLM debut this round.

Event Date: 2–4 October 2026 (falls within this edition's window; expo also ran the prior weekend)
Location: Singapore EXPO, Hall 6A/6B
Admission: Free
Best For: Families / Bargain Hunters / Food Lovers

Concierge Recommendation: A good free option to suggest to guests without a car – Singapore EXPO is directly linked to the MRT, and the free admission makes it an easy add-on to a Changi Airport transfer.

Smart Home Tech Show 2026

A consumer electronics showcase focused on smart home technology, with interactive demonstrations and show-only deals. SAFRA members receive an extra Sure-Win Draw chance and a $10 Show Cash Voucher with pre-registration.

Event Date: 1–4 October 2026
Location: Suntec Convention Centre
Admission: Free
Best For: Tech Enthusiasts / Homeowners

Concierge Recommendation: A niche pick, but worth mentioning to guests staying for an extended period who've asked about consumer electronics shopping in Singapore.

Also Continuing This Week

  • ERDINGER Oktoberfest – celebrations continue at Lau Pa Sat and venues island-wide through October, including limited-edition Oktoberfest Brew cans at major supermarkets and RedMart.

  • A Date with Tradition – Stamford Arts Centre's Night Festival tie-in exhibition runs through 3 October (10am–7pm); live weekend performances have concluded, but the exhibition installations remain on view.

  • ENHYPEN VR Concert: Destiny – closes 4 October at Golden Village Bugis+; guests attending from 27 September get an upgraded merchandise set over the earlier run.

The Weeknd – After Hours Til Dawn Stadium Tour

The Canadian superstar brings the Asia leg of his After Hours Til Dawn Stadium Tour to Singapore for two nights, with Japanese hip-hop duo Creepy Nuts as support. This is a full National Stadium production – expect heavy crowds and traffic build-up around Kallang on both nights, well beyond the immediate stadium precinct.

Event Date: 2–3 October 2026
Location: National Stadium, Singapore Sports Hub
Admission: Ticketed, via Ticketmaster (from $158)
Best For: Pop & R&B Fans

Concierge Recommendation: Flag this early to guests staying near the Sports Hub or East Coast – advise leaving significantly more time for taxis and ride-hailing on both nights, and expect Kallang-area roads and the Stadium MRT station to be very congested from late afternoon.

Also Playing This Week

  • Itzy – Tunnel Vision World Tour, Singapore Indoor Stadium, 3 October. Tickets from $158 via Ticketmaster.

  • Xlov – The Star Theatre, 1 October. Tickets from $142 via Sistic; Cat 1 sold out.

  • Shaggy – The Star Theatre, 2 October. Tickets from $78 via Sistic.

  • Bang Yong-guk (formerly of B.A.P) – Esplanade Annexe Studio, 3 October. Tickets from $100 via Sistic.

Looking Ahead – Formula 1 Singapore Grand Prix

Road closures for the Formula 1 Singapore Airlines Singapore Grand Prix begin at 12:01am on Wednesday, 7 October – just after this edition's window closes – and run through 5:30am on Tuesday, 13 October, covering the Marina Centre and Padang area. The race itself runs 9–11 October and will be Singapore's first-ever Sprint weekend. Hotel rates and occupancy across Marina Bay, Orchard Road, and the Civic District typically climb well before the race, so it's worth setting guest expectations on both pricing and access from early October onward. Full details will follow in next week's edition.

Restaurants & Bars

Sabòr

A new Spanish bodega-style concept on Boon Tat Street, leaning into comfort-food classics rather than fine-dining tapas – the kind of casual, sharing-plate spot suited to a relaxed group dinner.

Location: Boon Tat Street
Best For: Groups / Casual Dining / Spanish Cuisine Fans

Concierge Recommendation: A good alternative recommendation for guests who've already done the CBD's more familiar wine-bar circuit and want something with a different regional focus.

Singapore Martini Club

A new bar at Orchard Rendezvous Hotel built around a vintage luxury train-carriage theme, with more than 50 martinis on the menu – including zero-proof versions – organised into different “stops” from fruity to spirit-forward.

Location: Orchard Rendezvous Hotel
Signature: Tokyo Spice Martini (tequila, Japanese spices); Sub-Zero Dirty Martini (served tableside at around -10°C)
Best For: Cocktail Enthusiasts / Date Night / Small Groups

Concierge Recommendation: A strong pick for guests wanting a distinctive bar experience without leaving the Orchard Road area – the tableside Sub-Zero preparation is a genuine talking point.

Special Mention: From Shangri-La's Restaurant Recommendation List

Two picks this week from Shangri-La Singapore's own curated list of recommended restaurants across the city:

Min Jiang at Dempsey

Housed in a stylish black-and-white one-storey colonial building on Dempsey Hill, Min Jiang at Dempsey pairs Cantonese and Sichuan cooking with a genuinely distinctive setting – floor-to-ceiling windows, rattan furniture, and a timber-decked alfresco terrace looking onto the surrounding greenery. The Beijing duck, grilled in a wood-fired oven, is the dish regulars build a visit around.

Current Promotion: None advertised – check for seasonal set menus.

Reservation Policy: No credit card required to book; reserve via TableCheck or by phone.

Hours: Monday to Sunday. Lunch & Dim Sum 11:30am–2:30pm; Dinner 6:30pm–10:30pm.

Address: 7A & 7B Dempsey Road, Singapore 249684

Website: https://www.goodwoodparkhotel.com/dining/min-jiang-dempsey

Signature: Beijing Duck (wood-fire oven); Turbot Fish Two Ways; assorted dim sum

Concierge Recommendation: A strong pick for guests who want a proper sit-down Chinese meal in a garden setting rather than a hotel dining room – request the alfresco terrace for anyone who asks for something scenic.

Sarai

A contemporary Thai fine-dining room at Tanglin Mall built around สำรับ (sumrub), the traditional Thai style of dining once favoured by Thailand's royal family. Isan-born Chef de Cuisine Chimkit Khamphuang – known to regulars as Chef Lisa – draws on more than 27 years of experience to bring an elevated, personal take on Thai heritage cooking rather than the usual casual-Thai formula.

Current Promotion: None advertised – check for seasonal set menus.

Reservation Policy: No credit card required to book.

Hours: Monday to Sunday, 11:30am–3:00pm; 5:30pm–10:30pm (last order 9:30pm).

Address: 163 Tanglin Road, #03-122, Tanglin Mall, Singapore 247933

Website: https://www.sarai.com.sg/

Signature: Sumrub set menus; Goong Sarong (crispy prawns, Thai chilli sauce)

Concierge Recommendation: A good recommendation for guests who've already tried Singapore's casual Thai spots and want to see the fine-dining side of the cuisine – mention the sumrub format specifically, since it's not something most guests will have encountered.

Hotel & Hospitality News

  • Capitol Kempinski Hotel Singapore has appointed Anita Ngan as Director of Sales & Marketing. Ngan brings nearly two decades of experience in luxury hospitality to the role.

Transport & Operational Updates

No road closures fall within this edition's window. Expect heavy crowds and congestion around the Kallang / Singapore Sports Hub area on the evenings of 2 and 3 October, driven by The Weeknd's two-night stadium show – taxis and ride-hailing will be harder to get in that area both nights. Formula 1 road closures begin the following week, from 7 October – see “Looking Ahead” under Events & Festivals for details to start briefing guests on now.

Suggested Itineraries

A Food-Focused Saturday

Morning: Start at Tiong Bahru Market for a classic hawker breakfast, then browse the neighbourhood's independent bookshops and cafes.

Afternoon: Head to Singapore EXPO for TLM Food Expo (2–4 October only) – free admission, and a good two-to-three-hour browse for guests who enjoy food markets.

Evening: Return to the city for dinner at Sabòr on Boon Tat Street, then a nightcap at Origin Bar back at the hotel.

Tip: TLM Food Expo is a 15-minute taxi ride from Changi Airport – a good stop for guests with a late afternoon flight and a free morning.

A Cultural Sunday

Afternoon: Drop by Esplanade for the closing weekend of Octoburst! 2026 – free family programming continues through 4 October.

Late Afternoon: Walk along the Esplanade waterfront towards Marina Bay, taking in the skyline before the evening crowds arrive.

Evening: Dinner at The Rose Veranda for the last weekend of the Hong Kong Cha Chaan Teng series (closes 4 October), or Shang Palace for A Cantonese Expression of Korea's Finest.

Tip: Reserve The Rose Veranda ahead – it's a small 74-seat venue and the last weekend of a promotion tends to draw a crowd.

Quick Reference

Best Concert Pick: The Weeknd – After Hours Til Dawn Stadium Tour (National Stadium, 2–3 October)

Best Last-Chance Pick: The Rose Veranda's Hong Kong Cha Chaan Teng series (closes 4 October)

Best New Restaurant: Sabòr

Best New Bar: Singapore Martini Club

Best Free Family Activity: Octoburst! 2026 at Esplanade

Best Free Food Event: TLM Food Expo

Best Race-Season Pick: Grand Prix Season Singapore – Music Matters Live (Clarke Quay, free)

Looking Ahead: Formula 1 Singapore Grand Prix road closures begin 7 October; GPSS programming builds through the following week
